topic: Figma Prototyping and Interactive UI Design
learningObjectives: Identify the core workflow for creating interfaces in Figma.
Connect interface screens into interactive prototypes.
Apply components and reusable design elements to prototype screens.

activities.title: Figma Workspace Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the major areas of a Figma design workspace.

content.concept: A Figma workspace includes areas for navigating files and pages, editing the canvas, managing layers and properties, and creating prototype interactions.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Provides tools for creating and editing design objects.
Shows the hierarchy of frames, groups, components, and layers.
The main workspace where interface designs and frames are arranged.
Displays properties such as dimensions, layout, typography, fills, and effects.
Allows designers to define connections and interactions between prototype frames.

activities.title: Component System Builder
activities.instruction: Build a reusable UI component from its essential parts.

content.concept: Figma components allow repeated interface patterns to share a common structure and design. Variants can represent different states or properties of a component.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Prototype Flow
activities.instruction: Explore the parts required to connect screens into an interactive prototype.

content.concept: A prototype connects frames through user-triggered interactions. A trigger starts the interaction, an action determines what happens, and the destination identifies where the user goes when navigation is involved.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The event that starts an interaction, such as clicking or tapping an element.
The behavior performed after the trigger, such as navigating or opening an overlay.
The target frame or screen reached by a navigation interaction.
Defines how the prototype visually moves from one state or frame to another.

activities.title: Interaction Selector
activities.instruction: Choose the interaction that best fits each interface behavior.

content.concept: Prototype interactions should represent the intended user behavior, such as navigating to another screen, opening an overlay, changing a component state, or providing feedback.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
